messages:
Anya: FYI customer reported a weird one — they rotated an API key via Vault ~10m ago but some of their requests are still succeeding with the old key. filing an escalation. tenant=tenant-abc, route=/v1/generate, edge region=us-west.

mike_c: can you paste an example curl that succeeds vs one that fails? and the rotation job id?

Anya: rotation job id: rot-2026-03-15-11:02 (Vault transit rewrap + secret update). here's a quick repro I ran from my laptop:

# works (unexpected)
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer OLD_KEY_abc123" https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/generate
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
X-Cache: HIT from-edge
Content-Type: application/json
{ "id": "gen_...", "choices": [...] }

# fails at origin when forced
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer OLD_KEY_abc123" -H "Cache-Control: no-cache" https://api-internal.redwood.example.com/v1/generate
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
Content-Type: application/json
{ "error": "invalid_api_key" }

Anya: so edge returns 200, origin returns 401 with the same key.

sre_oncall: that's almost always a caching/keying problem on the CDN/edge. either Authorization isn't in the cache key and stale response was cached, or the edge isn't forwarding the header to origin on cache-miss/validate. any edge logs?

Anya: attaching an edge log snippet (redacted):

[2026-03-15T11:05:12Z] request_id=xyz edge_hit=true route=/v1/generate tenant=tenant-abc auth_checked=false cache_key=route:/v1/generate:tenant-abc status=200
[2026-03-15T11:06:01Z] request_id=xyz2 edge_hit=false forwarded_to_origin status=401 origin_msg="invalid key"

Anya: note the first line shows auth_checked=false which looked odd.

support_lead: @mike_c can we confirm what the CDN config uses as cache key? last infra change added some fast-path caching. @infra-bot do we have the VCL snippet or ingress config handy?

infra-bot: deploy-bot: recent PR 4852 changed edge cache key for /v1/generate to exclude Authorization header to improve hit rate. Link: https://git.internal/pr/4852

mike_c: ok that PR explains it. the tradeoff was to improve cache efficiency, but it means revoked keys can stay effective until TTL or explicit purge. what's the expected TTL on that route? is there a surrogate-key or purge hook on rotation events?

Anya: TTL is 5m. but the customer rotated at 11:02 and started seeing successes at 11:10 — beyond TTL. logs show X-Cache: HIT at 11:15. possible persistent cache because the cache was primed by a longer-surviving object or the edge used a different keying (maybe normalized URL removed tenant param). We also saw a Set-Cookie from origin earlier which might cause edge to treat response as cacheable.

sre_oncall: three action buckets: immediate mitigation (purge), short-term config patch (prevent auth-sensitive routes from excluding Authorization), long-term lifecycle (rotation -> purge automation).

support_lead: immediate: can you try a targeted purge for tenant-abc and route /v1/generate? use the CDN admin API and also invalidate any surrogate keys. customer is impacted.

mike_c: issuing purge now (CDN API):

auth curl -X POST "https://cdn-admin.redwood.example.com/purge" -H "Authorization: Bearer INFRA_TOKEN" -d '{"surrogate_key":"tenant-abc:/v1/generate"}'

infra-bot: purge accepted. purge_id=pge-9987. Estimated propagation 30-90s.

Anya: did a quick smoke after purge with old key — returns 401 now. sending to customer.

Anya: they confirmed failures for old key now. so purge fixed immediate impact.

mike_c: for root cause: PR 4852 removed Authorization from cache key. that improved cache efficiency but was a mismatch for endpoints where tokens can be revoked. when token revocation happens we also need to either include Authorization in cache key or ensure rotation triggers a purge.

sre_oncall: proposed fix: revert the exclusion for /v1/generate (and any auth-required dynamic endpoints) and add a note in the PR explaining cache impact. alternatively, keep exclusion but add rotation -> CDN purge hook in the rotation job.

support_lead: I'd prefer rotation->purge as lower latency cost, but we need to be robust if purges fail. do we have idempotent rotation events that can be consumed by CDN? maybe post to pubsub.

mike_c: we can add a post-rotate webhook in the vault rotation Lambda that posts to "infra-purge" topic with tenant id + routes. infra will subscribe and call CDN purge.

sre_oncall: also add monitoring: when a rotation occurs, run a healthcheck call to the edge with the old key; expect 401. if still 200, auto-purge and alert.

Anya: quick notes on reproduction for docs:
1) Rotate API key via vault (transit rewrap + update secret store). note rotation job id.
2) Repeat request hitting CDN (no Cache-Control) — if CDN cache key excludes Authorization you'll see old-key accepted until purge/TTL.
3) Force origin check by adding Cache-Control: no-cache, or call internal origin endpoint; will show 401.

sre_oncall: commands/logs we used here:
- vault list secret/data/tenants/tenant-abc
- kubectl logs deploy/rotation-worker -n infra | grep rot-2026-03-15-11:02
- curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer OLD_KEY_abc123" https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/generate
- curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer OLD_KEY_abc123" -H "Cache-Control: no-cache" https://api-internal.redwood.example.com/v1/generate
- CDN purge API: POST /purge { surrogate_key }

mike_c: config PR plan:
- short term: change edge config to include Authorization in cache key for /v1/** and /chat/** routes that validate per-token, add a comment and link to rotation flow.
- medium term: implement rotation -> pubsub -> purge hook in rotation job (Vault worker emits event). retry and dead-letter on failure.
- long term: consider short-lived ephemeral tokens + signature-based cache keys (eg: cache on tenant+signature-scheme) to avoid Authorization being cached while still benefiting from CDN.

support_lead: I've created a ticket INFRA-1224 to track PR + rotation hook + runbook updates. assign @mike_c and @sre_oncall.

Anya: customer updated: "thanks — old key invalid now and we're unblocked" :white_check_mark:

mike_c: added a one-liner to rotation playbook: "Always include CDN purge for tenant-scoped key rotations or ensure Authorization is in cache key for those routes." also linking this thread.

sre_oncall: follow-up: double-check we don't accidentally add Authorization to cache key for public static assets. only apply to authenticated API routes.

Anya: closing the escalation. lessons learned saved to KB: kb/internal/cdn-rotation-purge.md and added to new-rotation runbook.

deploy-bot: PR 4869 merged to revert cache-exclusion for /v1/generate; rollout scheduled 2026-03-15T13:00 UTC. :rocket:

infra-bot: INFRA-1224 updated: status=in-progress, assignees=[mike_c, sre_oncall].

Anya: thanks everyone. tagging here in case any downstream teams need context. :eyes:
